title: [recoverability] The recoverability north star counts the critical resources whose restore drill passed in the last 7 days, with the newest session backup's and the oldest passed drill's ages
prompt:
Read sync/recovery.md (the recovery table: its rows and their drills), crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs (`record_verified`: the database drill's `backup.verified`), deploy/ (the root session-backup units: spawn-session-backup.service writes /var/backups/spawn-sessions/status.json, 0644, `at` in epoch seconds; spawn-session-backup-drill.service is the restore drill), and serve.rs's core-lines module (objective 084; 087's recoverability guardrails if they are in).

This comes after objective 084 (the Core lines frame), which must be in the tree. If 087 is in, its guardrails come first and these follow.

The problem (owner, 2026-11-12 13:30; sync/roadmap-effects.md, Recoverability). The recoverability north star is the number of critical resources with a restore that passed in the last 7 days. Today it is read by hand from recovery.md ("5 of 6; configuration and credentials has no drill"). The drills exist but report in three places:
- the database drill writes `backup.verified` records Spawn reads;
- the session backups' restore drill is a root systemd unit whose result only systemd holds;
- the session backups themselves write a status file.
Which resources count is the recovery table's decision, so the rows go in the Core lines file beside the ranges, not in code.

Required behaviour.
(a) core-lines.json may hold `recoverability` {drills: [{name, record?: <type>, unit?: <name>.service}], session_backup_status?: <path>}, read on every request like the ranges.
- A row with `record` "backup.verified": its last pass is the newest such record with ok true.
- A row with `unit`: it is read without root through `$SPAWN_SYSTEMCTL show <unit> -p Result,ExecMainStatus,ExecMainExitTimestamp --timestamp=unix` (SPAWN_SYSTEMCTL defaults to systemctl). It passed when Result is success and ExecMainStatus is 0, at its exit timestamp. A unit name other than [A-Za-z0-9@._-]+.service is never run.
- A row with neither has no drill.
- The answer lists `drills` [{name, source ("record <type>", "unit <name>", or null), passed_at_ms}] in the file's order.
(b) The figures:
- north star `recoverability.restores_passed` (count): the rows whose last pass is within the last 7 days; null with no rows;
- `recoverability.session_backup_age` ("Age of the newest session backup", ms): the answer's moment less the status file's `at`; null without one;
- `recoverability.oldest_drill_age` ("Age of the oldest passed drill", ms): the answer's moment less the oldest of the rows' last passes. Rows that never passed are left out (the north star counts them). Null with none.
(c) The Home card lists the drills under the recoverability row, each with its last pass or "no drill". Read off a screenshot.
Reading the units must not stall a request: bound each call's time, or keep the result for up to 60 s. No gate, integrator or deploy step reads any of it.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/093.sh. A passing database drill is seeded 3 h ago and a failed one 1 h ago. A fake systemctl knows three units: one passed 10 h ago, one failed, one passed 8 days ago. There is a row whose unit name is a shell command, a configuration row with no drill, and a status file 10 minutes old. `spawn serve` answers. Checks:
- (1) Through `GET /api/core-lines`:
  - drills, in order: the database at its passing record (not the failed one after it), the session files at the unit's exit, the failed unit null, the old unit at 8 days, the bad name null, and the configuration with no source;
  - the bad name never reaches systemctl.
- (2) restores_passed is 2. The session backup's age (10 min) and the oldest drill's age (8 days) lie between seed time and answer time.
It fails with 1 on f41cbcc1: /api/core-lines answers 404. Its throwaway stacks 084's throwaway (sync/obj-093/throwaway.diff).

For the live core-lines.json once this lands (a lead step, from recovery.md):
- the rows: the database (record backup.verified), the session files (unit spawn-session-backup-drill.service), the rest as the table says, and configuration and credentials with no drill;
- session_backup_status: /var/backups/spawn-sessions/status.json;
- ranges: restores passed at least the row count (6), session backup at most 30 min, oldest drill at most 7 days.
On 11-12 the session drill unit has not run yet (no exit timestamp), so it counts as not passed until its first daily run.

The product reason. "A loss costs minutes" is only true if each restore has been rehearsed lately. Today that is a hand count in a notes file; this makes it a figure that falls the day a drill stops passing. Monitoring only.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (084 and 087 among them) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour:
- a core-lines unit test of the drill rows (a passing and a failing record, a unit's three results, a refused name, no drill, outside 7 days) and of both ages;
- a test that a unit call is bounded.
